analysis.title: How will Fed rate hikes impact markets?
key_insights: UBS CIO expects the Fed to raise rates by 25bp in December 2026 and March 2027, though the risk of consecutive hikes has grown.
October US inflation came in stronger than expected, with headline CPI +0.4% MoM and core +0.3%, reinforcing the case for tightening.
The FOMC held the funds rate in October after a 25bp hike in September.

October FOMC minutes showed almost all officials saw further hikes as needed if the economy evolves as expected. A few said a more restrictive stance may be required, and two said a move larger than 25bp could be warranted if inflation proves persistent.
UBS believes US equities can withstand measured tightening, citing GDP growth near 2.5% annualized in H1 and 3.4% in Q3.
UBS forecasts S&P 500 earnings growth of around 15% in 2027, which should help equities absorb higher yields.
Recommendation is to stay invested in equities, diversify across regions, sectors and return drivers, and manage concentrated single-stock exposure.
Fixed income is rated Attractive, with a preference for intermediate average duration to add portfolio income.
The 10-year Treasury yield hit 5.36% intraday in early October, the highest since 2002, and has since eased to about 5.06%.
ISM Manufacturing PMI has been in expansion for ten consecutive months, and past downturns generally began at least two years after the Fed started hiking.

sector_views.rationale: Rated Attractive. Elevated starting yields offer portfolio income, with intermediate duration favored.
Stay invested and diversified. Resilient growth and earnings should offset moderate tightening.

earnings_insights: UBS forecasts S&P 500 earnings growth of around 15% in 2027 (UBS estimate).

risk_factors: Inflation proves more persistent, prompting consecutive hikes or a move larger than 25bp.
Higher yields and a more restrictive policy stance could pressure equities.

tension_points.bull_case: Resilient growth (Q3 GDP 3.4%) and about 15% S&P 500 EPS growth in 2027 let equities absorb measured 25bp hikes.
tension_points.bear_case: Risk of consecutive hikes has grown, and two FOMC participants said a move larger than 25bp could be warranted if inflation proves persistent.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Inflation proving more persistent, leading the Fed to hike by more than 25bp or on consecutive meetings.

theme_stances.key_argument: Measured tightening should not derail the US economy, and higher yields create opportunities for portfolio income.
theme_stances.evidence: We do not expect measured Fed tightening to derail the US economy
